speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly when your wrist pain started and if you've noticed any fever or skin lesions recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you notice any rash on your palms, soles, or trunk? Also, were you bitten by a tick during your recent camping trip in Minnesota?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your camping history and the specific violaceous lesions, did you notice a red bullseye rash on your body at any point? I also need to check if your blood work shows signs of inflammation, so REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count and Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count shows WBC 15,000 /μL (elevated), Hemoglobin 14 g/dL, Platelets 300,000 /μL. Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR) is not available in current data; NORMAL READINGS for ESR. Additional findings: Joint aspiration of left wrist reveals WBC >50,000 /μL (markedly elevated) with Gram-negative diplococci on Gram stain; STI screen positive for Gonorrhea.

speaker: Doctor
text: The joint aspiration showing Gram-negative diplococci and your positive STI screen confirm you have Disseminated Gonococcal Infection. DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection (DGI) with septic arthritis.
